card_quote: Default disposition: gives gift cards, food or drink; thinks novelty books end up unread on a shelf; default answer to 'would you buy this as a gift' is no. / Narrative: Wants the gift done in five minutes and not to be embarrassing.
how_read: Honestly I'd look at the cover, read the how-to-play page and try the first round because you asked. I did round one on the couch with the game on. After that I'd flip the back pages to see if there's a scoresheet or anything. Wouldn't keep going on my own.

w1_friction.note: I turn the page expecting 'FOLKLORE, here's why' in two lines and get a whole essay. Nobody at an office party is reading that.
w1_friction.quote: The record separates the principle from the anecdote.

w1_friction.note: Fine, the apple didn't hit him. Did that need six paragraphs?
w1_friction.quote: The bump spread because it improves the story as a story.

w1_friction.note: Same apple twice in a row, and now it's telling me the skeptic is the dummy. Felt like a gotcha.
w1_friction.quote: The popular version here is a skeptic’s one.

w1_friction.note: This is the kind of answer where you're technically wrong and nobody cares. The idea was in there, just not the letters.
w1_friction.quote: The statement survives the check; the typography does not.

w1_friction.note: 'Disputed' is a cop-out answer for a quiz. Either it's true or it isn't.
w1_friction.quote: Who first said it, and in what words, is not settled.

w1_best.why: Einstein's Nobel for the photoelectric thing. Short version is a good bar fact.
I'd have said 'blood, sweat and tears' too. Fair catch.
I work around tech people and they all say 18 months. Good to know it's wrong.
Didn't know the tower thing was a legend. Ramps and water clocks, ok.
Easy one, but at least it's quick to get.

w1_flat.why: The apple again. Felt like a filler question.
Splitting hairs over how a formula was written.
Too long for what it is, and it opens the book on a lecture.
Kind of figured nobody really 'discovers' a math rule alone. Wasn't surprised.

w1_review.headline: Good idea, way too much reading
w1_review.body: The guessing part is fun for about ten questions. Every answer is a page of dense text, so it's more of a book than a game, and some answers just say nobody knows. I could see one specific nerdy person liking it. Bottom line: not my kind of gift; I'll stick with a gift card.

w2_review_first: It's one of those 'everything you know is wrong' books, but long-winded. If you know someone who reads Wikipedia for fun, maybe. Otherwise skip it.

w2_lost.why: First answer was a wall of text and I checked my phone.
Second apple question in a row, that's where I mentally checked out.
Finished round one and had no reason to start round two.

w2_read_aloud.why: Streisand suing over her house photo is funny and everyone's heard of the Streisand thing.
Butter-side-down toast, people will argue about that.
Monty Hall always starts a fight. People get heated.
Work crowd would bite on the Moore's law one.
The Kitty Genovese 38 witnesses thing, I remember that from school. Would be good to know.

w2_cut.why: Latin quote from a monk. No.
Never heard of Hebb. Can't guess on something you've never heard of.
Yerkes and Dodson, no idea who that is.
Thomas Young and slits, too sciencey.
Duplicate of the other apple question.

w2_book2: I wouldn't have bought the first one, so a second one is a no unless the answers got down to a few lines.
